candidate.answerReason: After 15 minutes, the cars are 7 and 10 miles from A. Both then travel at 40 mph, so they meet halfway between those positions, at 8.5 miles from A.

methods.label: Track entry into the middle portion
methods.explanation:
Track when each car enters the middle portion, because both cars then have the same speed. The car from \(A\) takes
\[
\frac{5}{25}\cdot60=12\text{ minutes}
\]
to travel its first \(5\) miles. The car from \(B\) takes
\[
\frac{5}{20}\cdot60=15\text{ minutes}
\]
to travel its first \(5\) miles.

Between minutes \(12\) and \(15\), the car from \(A\) travels at \(40\) mph for \(3\) minutes, covering
\[
40\cdot\frac{3}{60}=2\text{ miles}.
\]
Thus, at minute \(15\), that car is \(5+2=7\) miles from \(A\), while the other car is \(15-5=10\) miles from \(A\). They are still apart, and both are now traveling at \(40\) mph in the middle portion.

Since their speeds are equal, they cover equal shares of the remaining \(3\)-mile gap. They meet at
\[
7+\frac{10-7}{2}=8.5
\]
miles from \(A\). This point is within the middle portion, so neither car changes speed again before meeting. The answer is \(8.5\) miles, choice \(\mathrm{D}\).
methods.levelReason: Uses distance, speed, elapsed time, hour-to-minute conversion, and an equal division of a gap, all within AMC 8 arithmetic and spatial reasoning.

methods.label: Halve the full-road travel time
methods.explanation:
The useful observation is that driving any portion of this road takes the same time in either direction. A car driving the entire road at the speed limits would need
\[
\frac{5}{25}\cdot60=12,\qquad
\frac{5}{40}\cdot60=7.5,\qquad
\frac{5}{20}\cdot60=15
\]
minutes for the three portions, totaling \(34.5\) minutes.

At the meeting point, the two cars have traveled for equal times, and their traveled portions together make the whole road. Because each portion takes the same time in either direction, the full-road travel time is twice their meeting time. Therefore, they meet after
\[
34.5\div2=17.25\text{ minutes}.
\]
The car from \(A\) finishes the first portion after \(12\) minutes and would finish the middle portion after \(12+7.5=19.5\) minutes. Thus it is in the middle portion when they meet. It spends \(17.25-12=5.25\) minutes there, so its distance from \(A\) is
\[
5+40\cdot\frac{5.25}{60}
=5+3.5=8.5\text{ miles}.
\]
The answer is \(8.5\) miles, choice \(\mathrm{D}\).
methods.levelReason: Uses additive travel times and elementary arithmetic. The time-halving observation requires no equation-solving or advanced rate machinery.

candidate.annotationRationale: The target is locating an opposite-direction meeting when speeds change by road portion. Both methods use the distance-speed-time relationship, its inverse for finding time, and time-unit conversion. The first method additionally uses a midpoint after synchronizing the cars' positions. The second uses the distinct observation that the meeting divides the full-road travel time equally. Neither written method requires linear-equation procedures.
